audits.title: An Audit to Improve Prescription Writing on Inpatient Medication Cards
audits.standard: Basic standards of prescription writing; target 100%

cycle1.result: Significant deficiency in prescription writing (no figures given).

audits.intervention: Results presented at internal teaching to all doctors with recommendations.

cycle2.result: Improvement in prescription writing and recording (no figures given).

audits.other_findings: Recommended repeat audit every six months.
audits.citation: Parvathaiah H, Osman F, Daly C. An Audit to Improve Prescription Writing on Inpatient Medication Cards. European Psychiatry. 2016;33(S1):S437-S437. doi:10.1016/j.eurpsy.2016.01.1588.

audits.title: Time to Rectify the Neglect? Audit on Prescription Writing the Neglected skill. Audit Ref No: AU/006/01/2021
audits.standard: BMA, BNF and Trust prescription writing standards (GMC number, signature, doctor's name, drug, indication, dose, route, frequency, start date, date, timings)
audits.setting: Victoria Ward, old age psychiatry, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Errors found in all parameters except medication timings

audits.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting and re-training on prescription writing

cycle2.result: Errors increased: GMC number errors up 20.33%, doctor's name 16.87%, indication 12.94%, original start date 5%; name of drug improved by 10.88%

audits.other_findings: Trust then issued stamps with GMC number and doctor's name to junior doctors; re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Fulmali A, Sheik S, Suleman A, Rana F, Bloxam R, Abdallah L, et al.. Time to Rectify the Neglect? Audit on Prescription Writing the Neglected skill. Audit Ref No: AU/006/01/2021. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S154-S154. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.437.

audits.title: Assessing Improvement in Prescription Writing Quality in Adult Male and Female Wards of Psychiatry Department, Lahore, Pakistan: Three Cycles of Clinical Audit
audits.setting: Adult male and female psychiatry wards, Lahore

cycle1.result: Generic names used in 40.6%; block letters 17%; start date recorded 82.8%.

audits.intervention: Presentation of BNF prescription-writing guidelines on 7 December 2022 and copies placed at male and female nursing counters.

cycle2.result: Generic names used in 84.69%; block letters 71.42%; start date recorded 99.18%.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles; an interim re-audit (December 2022, 170 prescriptions) showed improvement but documentation of prescription changes still needed work. Legibility stayed high throughout.
audits.citation: Khan A, Arif U, Shahzad A, Tahir S, Khan R. Assessing Improvement in Prescription Writing Quality in Adult Male and Female Wards of Psychiatry Department, Lahore, Pakistan: Three Cycles of Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S261-S261. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.629.

audits.title: Audit and Re-audit on Inpatient Prescription Writing in Psychiatry Ward of Allied Hospital 2 Faisalabad
audits.setting: Psychiatry ward, Allied Hospital 2, Faisalabad, tertiary care hospital

cycle1.result: 156 charts with 624 prescriptions showed severe discrepancies, including missing dose, frequency, strength and start/end dates.

audits.intervention: Faculty-led workshop and mandatory teaching sessions for residents on prescription documentation.

cycle2.period: About three months later (dates not reported)
cycle2.result: 200 charts with 650 prescriptions showed much improvement in all highlighted areas (figures not reported).

audits.citation: Fatima D, Dogar I, Sajid P, Fatima S, Jelani S. Audit and Re-audit on Inpatient Prescription Writing in Psychiatry Ward of Allied Hospital 2 Faisalabad. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S230-S230. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10576.

audits.title: Improving Prescribing Documentation in a Community Learning Disability Team: A Clinical Audit and SOP (Standard Operating Procedure) Development
audits.standard: Local prescribing documentation standards (upload to Care Director, clinic register entry, case note documentation)
audits.setting: Community Learning Disability Team, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 65% (208/319) of prescriptions uploaded to Care Director; 19% (58/300, clozapine excluded) entered in clinic register; documented elsewhere in 98% (314/319).

audits.intervention: Standard Operating Procedure: scan-first requirement, legibility standards, mandatory case-note entry of medication and dose, centralised electronic tracking register, quarterly monitoring and data protection guidance.
audits.other_findings: 319 prescriptions to 147 patients from 297 records reviewed; documentation was frequent but inconsistent in format, location and completeness; re-audit recommended at 6–12 months.
audits.citation: Mathur S. Improving Prescribing Documentation in a Community Learning Disability Team: A Clinical Audit and SOP (Standard Operating Procedure) Development. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S317-S317. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11668.
